statement: WeChat Pay signing helpers (calculate_signature, dict_to_xml) live in wechatpy/pay/utils.py, and pay API modules such as wechatpy/pay/api/order.py sign request data with calculate_signature(data, self._client.api_key).
The WeChat Pay signature covers every field in the payload except sign, so an extra field such as return_msg that was not included when signing makes signature verification fail.
quote: The `check_signature` works correctly (my earlier "plain XML" failure was just my test adding an unsigned `return_msg` field).

statement: Python-exposed xmlsec constants (KeyData, Transform, namespaces, etc.) are registered in src/constants.c with macros like PYXMLSEC_ADD_KEYDATA_CONSTANT and PYXMLSEC_ADD_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT, and optional features are wrapped in #ifndef XMLSEC_NO_* guards (e.g. XMLSEC_NO_XKMS).

The bundled xmlsec-xmlsec-1_2_30 directory has only docs and examples, so the extension builds against the system xmlsec1 headers in /usr/include/xmlsec1 (version 1.2.37 in this environment); `xmlsec1-config --cflags` shows the feature macros such as XMLSEC_NO_GOST.

sanic_routing exports BaseRouter (abstract, with abstract `get`), not Router; to use it you subclass it and implement get(path, method, extra=None) by calling self.resolve(path=path, method=method, extra=extra), the same way tests/conftest.py does.
quote: BaseRouter is abstract. Let me check the tests' conftest to see how they instantiate a router.
